title: Reserves on a Host Payout Account and the Figure a Claim Is Opened At
content:
What the marketplace holds in reserve against a host, and whether money is currently stopped on that host's account, settles how much of the figure a Keyturn Host Protection Plan claim is opened at.

The marketplace's provisioned-exposure mark is 1000.

- Where the reserves standing on the host's payout account are below the marketplace's provisioned-exposure mark and money is currently stopped on that account, the figure is opened at the stopped-exposure share, which is 75 percent.
- Where those reserves are below that mark and no money is stopped on the account, it is opened at the unprovisioned-exposure share, which is 90 percent.
- Where those reserves reach that mark, it is opened in full.

### Both sides of the mark

| Reserves on the account | Money stopped on the account | The figure is opened at |
|---|---|---|
| below 1000 | yes | 75 percent of it |
| below 1000 | no | 90 percent of it |
| 1000 or more | either | the whole of it |

Reserves of exactly 1000 reach the mark, and the figure is opened in full whether or not money is stopped on the account; reserves of 999 do not reach it.

### The records behind the reading

The reserves standing on the account and whether money is currently stopped on it are read from the host's Keyturn Host Payout Account. Money is stopped where a ground for stopping it stands recorded against that account, and no such ground means no money is stopped.
